extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, appellants, agency representatives, D.C. Bar members, court reporters, and court clerks who practice before or administer rules of the District of Columbia Court of Appeals and the D.C. Bar
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing the District of Columbia Bar (membership classes, mandatory training, governance, fees, disbursements, bylaws, public statements, referendum) together with Court of Appeals procedural rules on records on appeal, transmission, petitions for review, in forma pauperis procedures, computing time, and related appellate filing/transmission duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects and purposes of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall promote the proper professional interests of members; encourage formation and support of volunteer bar associations; provide a forum and publish information about the practice of law, jurisprudence, law reform, and the Bar's relationship to the public; carry on continuing legal research and education in substantive law, practice and procedure; and make reports and recommendations so the public responsibility of the legal profession may be effectively discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists multiple core functions the Bar must carry out (education, publication, support of bar activities, research, recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership inclusion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of the Bar of the District of Columbia Court of Appeals shall be members of the District of Columbia Bar subject to compliance with membership conditions and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Bylaws and District of Columbia Bar Membership Manual. Residence in D.C. is not a condition of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory course for new admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: Within twelve months after admission to the Bar, all members must complete a course on the District of Columbia Rules of Professional Conduct and on District of Columbia practice and certify compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete or satisfy related requirements may result in suspension and inability to practice in D.C. The Bar must report annually to the Court addressing curriculum, faculty, number of presentations, attendance, and number of attorneys suspended for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of membership (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members shall be divided into at least four classes: active, judicial, inactive, and retired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rule enumerates each class and establishes that additional classes may be created by the Board after consultation with the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactive membership eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Inactive members are those eligible for active membership but not engaged in the practice of law in D.C. and who have submitted a written request to enroll as inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inactive members in good standing may change classification to active by written request and paying active license fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial membership classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial members include judges of courts of record, full-time court commissioners, U.S. bankruptcy judges, U.S. magistrate judges, other persons who perform a judicial function exclusively in an official capacity, and retired judges eligible for temporary judicial assignment and not engaged in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If terms of employment require eligibility to practice law, the member may choose to be an active member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired membership eligibility and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired members are those who have retired from practice (except for pro bono under D.C. App R. 49), or who are totally disabled and unable to practice, and who certify: (a) five years of active membership (with substitution rules: two years of any combination of inactive or judicial membership may substitute for one year of active membership), and (b) a total of 25 years engaged in the practice of law in D.C. or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in Rule 49(c), judicial, inactive, or retired members are not entitled to practice law in D.C., hold office, vote in general elections, or vote on Bar business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing classification to active
rubrics_metrics.description: Inactive members in good standing and judicial members who are no longer judges may change classification to active by submitting a written request to the Bar and paying the license fees required of active members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial members who are no longer judges shall be classified as active if they engage in practice in D.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to create additional membership classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may, after consultation with the Court, create additional classes of membership and establish required qualifications for those classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary upon Board action and Court consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: License fee ceiling and Board/ Court roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall set a ceiling for annual license fees payable by any member; the Board of Governors shall determine the amount to be paid annually by members in various classes; all fees are paid to the Bar for its expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board recommendations to the Court about the ceiling shall be published and members have 60 days (or other period the Court directs) to comment. Recommendations by the Board to increase the ceiling are not subject to referendum under Rule VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-payment of license fees consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-payment of license fees may result in suspension and inability to practice law in the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative enforcement consequence; no additional guidance provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and reinstatement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Resignation from and reinstatement into the Bar are governed by procedures prescribed by the Bar, which shall include consultation with the Office of Disciplinary Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures are set by the Bar (not specified in detail here) and must consult Disciplinary Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to the Clerk of membership changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Bar shall forward immediately to the Clerk of the Court the names of attorneys who have registered with the Bar and those whose membership status has changed pursuant to the Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative duty for prompt notification to the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers eligibility, terms, and compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of the Bar (President, President-Elect, Secretary, Treasurer) shall be nominated and elected or appointed as provided in the Bylaws; only active members are eligible; term of office is one year; officers receive no compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties of officers and vacancy process are described in the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Governors composition and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Affairs of the Bar are managed by a Board of Governors consisting of the officers, the Immediate Past-President, and fifteen members elected as prescribed by the Bylaws; the Treasurer-Elect is among the fifteen elected non-officer members and becomes at-large member after completing a year as Treasurer; the Board may appoint non-voting members as prescribed in the Bylaws and has general charge of affairs in accordance with these Rules and Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board governs Bar activities consistent with Rules and Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public statements authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion of the Bar on any matter involving legislation of major public interest or concern or of major importance to the members of the Bar shall be publicly expressed unless authorized by the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes authority for public positions in the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an annual meeting of members in the manner prescribed by the Bylaws; special meetings shall be called as set forth in the Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and scheduling are delegated to the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may, by affirmative vote of two-thirds of the Board, refer any question of Bar policy to active members for determination by ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board-initiated referenda require a 2/3 Board vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum initiation by member petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit for member ballot any question of Bar policy, including proposals for Rule or Bylaw changes, when directed by a petition signed by not less than 3% of active members based on the census as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative threshold (3%) for member-initiated referendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballots shall be prepared, distributed, returned and counted per regulations prescribed by the Board; the result, determined by majority of votes cast, shall be published in the official Bar publication and shall control the action of the Bar, Board, officers, and committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of votes cast is binding; Board prescribes logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement responsibilities, accounting, and audit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall make necessary appropriations from treasury funds to pay expenses of the Bar, officers, employees, and committees; keep proper books of account; procure an annual audit by a certified public accountant; and present a financial statement at each annual meeting showing assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the financial statement must be transmitted to the Clerk and published prior to the annual meeting; the Clerk copy must be accompanied by a detailed statement reflecting all significant components of total disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaws adoption rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws not inconsistent with these Rules may be established by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two-thirds of voting Board members present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies quorum (two-thirds present) and majority requirement for bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment proposals to the Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to amend these Rules may be presented to the Court by petition of the Board of Governors; hearing upon such a petition is pursuant to notice as the Court may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board petitions Court for rule amendments; Court controls hearing notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of Bar Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Bar Rules shall take effect on April 1, 1972, on which date the association shall be deemed to have come into existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical effective date; administrative/archival detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record on appeal—composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The record on appeal consists of (1) the original papers and exhibits filed in the Superior Court; (2) the transcript of proceedings, if any; and (3) a certified copy of the docket entries prepared by the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three components together constitute the official record on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s duty to order transcript (Rule 10(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after filing the notice of appeal, the appellant (unless proceeding per Rule 10(b)(5)) must order from the reporter a transcript of such parts of the proceedings the appellant considers necessary and identify any transcript already prepared to be included, or file a certificate stating that no transcript will be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10-day deadline; choice to order transcript or file certificate; Rule 10(b)(5) exceptions for certain IFP proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for transcript when challenging findings (Rule 10(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant intends to urge that a finding or conclusion is unsupported by or contrary to the evidence, the appellant must include in the record a transcript of all evidence relevant to that finding or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Cobb v. Standard Drug Co., 453 A.2d 110 (D.C. 1982) as authority; ensures record sufficiency for appellate challenge to factual findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial transcript procedures (Rule 10(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the entire transcript is not ordered, the appellant must within 10 days file a statement of the issues and serve copies of transcript order/certificate and the statement; other parties have 10 days to designate additional parts; if appellant does not order those parts within 10 days after designation, the designating party may order them or move in Superior Court to require the appellant to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequenced deadlines: appellant statement within initial 10 days; designating party has 10 days after service to designate; appellant then has 10 days to order or else the designating party may act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment arrangements for transcripts (Rule 10(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of ordering, a party must make satisfactory arrangements with the Court Reporter Division for paying the cost of the transcript, except when the party is proceeding under Rule 10(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial responsibility at ordering time unless transcript is covered by IFP/CJA provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts in in forma pauperis or CJA appeals (Rule 10(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil appellants proceeding in forma pauperis (with waiver of fees under Rule 24) must request transcript preparation by motion to the appropriate judge; appellants permitted under the Criminal Justice Act have the notice of appeal treated as an order for preparation of the reporter’s transcript at government expense; counsel appointed under the Prevention of Child Abuse and Neglect Act must secure vouchers for transcript preparation for judge approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedures depending on how the waiver was granted; references to statute and forms and Special procedures indicated in Rule 24 and D.C. Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the evidence when transcript unavailable (Rule 10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transcript is unavailable, the appellant may prepare a statement of the evidence or proceedings from best available means (including recollection), serve it on other parties who may object or propose amendments within ten days, then submit the statement and objections/amendments to the trial judge for settlement and approval; as settled it is included by the Clerk in the record on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process substitutes for an official transcript when not available; trial judge settles the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed statement as record on appeal (Rule 10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may prepare, sign, and submit a statement of the case showing how the issues arose and were decided; the statement must set forth only facts essential to issues; if accurate, the trial judge may approve it (with additions if necessary) and it will be certified as the record on appeal. A copy may be filed instead of the appendix required by Rule 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual agreement can replace the formal record; trial judge approval required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or modification of the record (Rule 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences about what the record discloses must be submitted to and settled by the trial court and the record conformed accordingly; omissions or misstatements material to any party may be corrected and a supplemental record certified and forwarded either by stipulation of the parties or by the Superior Court before or after forwarding; all other questions as to form and content must be presented to this Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two mechanisms to correct record: stipulation or Superior Court action; other disputes to the Court of Appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s duty to enable assembly and forwarding of record (Rule 11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant filing a notice of appeal must comply with Rule 10(b) and do whatever is necessary to enable the Clerk of the Superior Court to assemble and forward the record. If multiple appeals arise from a judgment or order, the Clerk must assemble a single record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation on appellant to assist in record assembly; mandates a single record for multiple appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter’s duties on receiving transcript order (Rule 11(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving an order for a transcript, the reporter must enter the date of receipt and expected completion date at the bottom of the order, send a copy so endorsed to the Clerk of the Superior Court; if transcript cannot be completed within 60 days reporter may request additional time from this Court; when complete the reporter must file it with the Director of the Court Reporter Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented receipt and expected completion date; 60-day completion target with extension procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director of Court Reporter Division duties (Rule 11(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If not all transcripts ordered or designated for appeal are completed within 60 days, the Director must retain the partial transcript until all transcription is complete; when completed, the transcript must be placed in chronological sequence, pages renumbered, and filed with the Clerk of the Superior Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative duty to assemble and renumber multi-part transcripts into a complete, chronologically ordered transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of Superior Court duties for forwarding record (Rule 11(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the record is complete, the Clerk must prepare an index identifying and numbering documents constituting the record and promptly send four certified copies of the index and the original reporter’s transcript, if any, to the Clerk of this Court; the Clerk must retain other parts of the record for parties to use, subject to call by this Court. In IFP cases where a waiver was granted, the Clerk must prepare and submit two copies. If reporter’s transcript is filed after transmittal of the certified index, the Clerk must forward it as a supplemental record promptly after filing by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies number of certified copies (4 normally, 2 for certain IFP cases) and retention/forwarding rules for supplemental transcript filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record for preliminary motions in Court of Appeals (Rule 11(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party files a motion in this Court before the record is forwarded (e.g., dismissal, summary reversal/affirmance, release pending appeal, stay, injunction, etc.), the Clerk of the Superior Court, upon order of this Court, must transmit a preliminary record containing the notices of appeal, the order appealed from, and those parts of the record designated by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables transmission of a limited record for preliminary relief motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencing review of agency orders—petition filing (Rule 15(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of an agency order or decision is commenced by filing with the Clerk of this Court an original and six copies of a petition for review; two or more persons may join if joinder is practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing format requirement: original plus six copies; joinder allowed where interests align.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file petition for review (Rule 15(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a statute provides a different time frame, the petition for review must be filed within 30 days after notice is given in conformance with the agency’s rules; if statute prescribes less than 11 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays are excluded in computation unless statute provides otherwise; if notice is by mail from an out-of-presence proceeding, petitioner has 5 additional days from date of mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 30-day period with specified adjustments for short statutory periods and mailed notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of petition for review (Rule 15(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must (A) name each party seeking review either in the caption or body (generic terms like 'et al.' are insufficient); (B) name the agency as respondent; and (C) specify the order or decision or part to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict naming requirement to ensure parties and agency respondent are specifically identified; special rules for Office of Administrative Hearings cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) petition special rule (Rule 15(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: In OAH review cases the petition must name each party seeking review and specify the order or part to be reviewed; only the parties before OAH and any other party permitted to participate by this Court shall be parties in this Court. The petition may not name OAH or the Administrative Law Judge as respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites D.C. Code § 2-1831.16(h) for party limitations; emphasizes naming only parties from the agency proceeding as respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail filing timing rule (Rule 15(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing may be accomplished by mail addressed to the Clerk, but filing will not be deemed timely unless the petition is in fact received by the Clerk within the prescribed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt by Clerk is the determinative timeliness test for mailed filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate petitioner signature requirement (Rule 15(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner is a corporation or other entity, the petition must be signed by counsel; petitions lacking necessary signature will be stricken unless corrected promptly after being called to counsel’s or party’s attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural defenseable by correction if promptly remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-petition timing (Rule 15(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely petition for review is filed, any other party to the agency proceeding may file a cross-petition for review within 14 days after the petition was filed, or within 30 days of the date of the challenged order or decision, whichever period expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the later of two windows for filing cross-petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested form for petition (Rule 15(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 5 is a suggested form of a petition for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of Form 5 is suggested but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely petition for rehearing on filing deadline (Rule 15(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party timely files a petition for rehearing or reconsideration in accordance with the agency’s rules, the time to petition for review runs from the date when notice of the order denying the petition is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing deadline is tolled pending agency rehearing/reconsideration and restarts upon denial notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition and filing list (Rule 15(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clerk must serve a copy of the petition for review on each respondent agency and the Corporation Counsel/Office of the Attorney General or other counsel representing any agency respondent. At filing, the petitioner must serve a copy on each party admitted to participate in the agency proceedings (except agency respondents) and file with the Clerk a list of those so served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures agency counsel and other parties are served and that the Court has a filing list for service records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention in agency review (Rule 15(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the agency proceeding who wants to intervene in this Court must, within 30 days from the date the petition is filed, serve upon all parties and file with the Clerk a notice of intention to intervene, and will be deemed an intervenor without a motion. Any other person who wants to intervene must file a motion to intervene within 30 days unless time is extended for good cause; the motion must be served on all parties and contain a concise statement of the moving party's interest, grounds for intervention, and which side the party seeks to join.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates automatic intervention for agency parties and motion-based intervention for others; 30-day default window with possible extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for petition for review (Rule 15(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing any separate or joint petition for review, the petitioner must pay the Clerk all required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard filing fee requirement; no further elaboration on amounts here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 25.1 applicability to certain agency orders (Rule 15(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent applicable, Rule 25.1 (Emergency and Expedited Cases) governs review of certain agency orders or decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts parties to special emergency/expedited procedures where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to file record and time (Rule 17(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent agency must file the record within 60 days after being served with a petition for review. For OAH decisions, OAH must file within 60 days of an order directing filing. The court may shorten or extend these deadlines for good cause. The Clerk must notify parties and intervenors that the record has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 60-day default with court discretion to alter for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes filing of record (Rule 17(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must file (A) the original or a certified copy of the record on review or parts designated by the parties; or (B) if a partial record is filed, a certified list adequately describing all documents, transcripts, exhibits, and other material constituting the record on review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows full record or a certified list describing a partial record adequate to identify materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties’ stipulation re: record filing and agency retention (Rule 17(b)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may stipulate in writing that no record or certified list be filed; the date the stipulation is filed is treated as the filing date. The agency must retain any portion of the record not filed; retained parts remain part of the record and must be sent to the Court if requested regardless of prior stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulation can simplify filing but agency retains non-filed parts which remain part of the record for all purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: In forma pauperis waiver statutory standards (Rule 24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards governing eligibility for waiver are listed in D.C. Code § 15-712(a)(1)(A)-(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule refers applicants to statutory eligibility criteria rather than restating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from the Superior Court—prior approval for IFP (Rule 24(a)(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party permitted to proceed in forma pauperis, or granted a waiver of court fees, costs, or security in the Superior Court, or determined eligible for court-appointed counsel under specified statutes, may proceed on appeal in forma pauperis without further authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior Superior Court authorization carries forward to appellate proceedings in many situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior Court procedures for seeking waiver on appeal (Rule 24(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who desires to take an appeal without prepayment of fees, costs, or security must file in the Superior Court within the time for filing an appeal: (i) a notice of appeal (Form 1 or Form 2) and (ii) an application to waive court fees, costs, or security pursuant to Superior Court Rule of Civil Procedure 54-II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial waiver application process typically begins in Superior Court; timing ties to appeal filing deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Superior Court grant or denial of waiver and appellate remedy (Rule 24(a)(2)(B)-(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Superior Court grants the waiver, the party may proceed on appeal without prepaying fees or security. If the Superior Court denies the waiver in whole or in part, it must issue a written order stating reasons; within 10 days the party may request a hearing under the Superior Court rule, and if denied after hearing the party may file in this Court an application to proceed without paying fees including required copies and statements showing why the denial was in error and evidence of inability to proceed without substantial hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies administrative remedies and documentation required when Superior Court denies waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate motions to proceed IFP after paying fees (Rule 24(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks to proceed in forma pauperis after having filed a notice of appeal and paid the required fees, the party must file with this Court an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7a) and sign the declaration/affidavit (Form 7b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides route to seek waiver after initial fee payment rather than via Superior Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver when review proceeds directly to Court of Appeals (Rule 24(b)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When review of an agency order proceeds directly to this Court, a party may file in this Court, with the petition for review, an application to waive court costs, fees, or security (Form 7) and sign the declaration (Form 7). The waiver application and petition must be filed within the time permitted for seeking review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct-review petitions may include waiver requests contemporaneously with filing the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFP procedures for extraordinary writs (Rule 24(c)(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party filing a petition for an extraordinary writ and desiring to proceed IFP must file, along with the petition, an application to waive costs (Form 7a) and sign the declaration/affidavit (Form 7b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels waiver procedures for appeals and petitions; forms specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for deciding waiver applications (Rule 24(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 5 calendar days after receiving a completed waiver application, the court must decide whether to approve it. If the court has not ruled within 5 calendar days, the application will be deemed approved, except where the court requires additional information under D.C. Code § 15-712(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short statutory decision window; deemed approval if court fails to act within 5 days barring need for more info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of IFP waiver—written reasons and hearing (Rule 24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a waiver application is denied by this Court, the court shall state reasons for the denial or partial denial in writing. A party denied in whole or part may request a hearing under D.C. Code § 15-712(c)(3)(A); such a hearing must be held no later than 14 days after the court receives the hearing request. If after hearing the waiver is denied, the petitioner must pay the required filing fee within the time specified in the final order of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process protections: written reasons and an expedited hearing timeline when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits not to be considered in waiver decision (Rule 24(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering a waiver application, the court must not consider the merits of the appeal or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver decisions are to be made based on financial eligibility, not the substantive strength of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for free transcripts/documents—civil cases (Rule 24(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party in a civil case granted a waiver may file a motion in the Superior Court requesting that free transcripts or other documents be prepared and must explain the basis; the Superior Court must grant the motion unless frivolous. In determining frivolousness, the Superior Court must resolve doubt in favor of the applicant. The Superior Court may order that only portions necessary to resolution of the appeal be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low threshold to grant free transcripts in civil IFP cases; court may limit extent to what is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for free transcripts—criminal cases (Rule 24(h)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In criminal cases where appellant was permitted to proceed in the Superior Court under the Criminal Justice Act, the notice of appeal is treated as an order for transcript preparation at government expense. In other criminal cases, a defendant granted a waiver may file a motion in Superior Court requesting free transcripts/documents; such a motion will be treated as an order for transcript preparation at government expense and addressed under Rule 10(b)(5)(B) procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers CJA-appointed counsel and other criminal-waiver situations; follows Rule 10 special procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of waiver applications (Rule 24(i)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The court must keep confidential an application and any financial information submitted by the applicant, except to the court, the litigant, persons authorized by the litigant, or by court order. The application must not be served on the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants’ financial privacy; restricts distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for access to confidential waiver information (Rule 24(i)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person seeking access to an application or financial information may file a motion, with notice given to the litigant who filed the application, supported by a declaration showing good cause for release; any person granted access must not reveal information except as authorized by law or court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is possible but requires showing good cause and imposes nondisclosure obligations on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-confidentiality of court’s waiver decision (Rule 24(i)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The court’s decision on an application for a waiver shall not be confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome is public even though application materials are confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references for IFP special rules (Rule 24(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules specially governing in forma pauperis appeals proceeding without paying fees, costs, or security, see Rules 10(b)(5), 11(b)(3), and 30(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reader to related provisions governing transcripts, transmission in IFP cases, and appendix/brief appendix rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing time—exclude day of act (Rule 26(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude the day of the act, event, or default that begins the period when computing any period of time specified in these rules or in any order or statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard day-counting rule to start computation on the following day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing time—exclude intermediate weekends/holidays for short periods (Rule 26(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays when the period is less than 11 days, unless statute or order provides otherwise or the period is stated in calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short deadlines (<11 days) exclude weekends and holidays; otherwise include them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing time—include last day except certain closures (Rule 26(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the last day of the period unless it is a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday, or, if the act is filing a paper in court, a day on which the Clerk’s office is closed due to weather or other conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final-day rule with exceptions for office closures and weekends/holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of legal holiday for time computation (Rule 26(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Legal holiday’ includes New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King, Jr.’s Birthday, Presidents’ Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans’ Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and any other day appointed as a holiday by the President or Congress or by the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates holidays treated as legal holidays for timing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending time for good cause (Rule 26(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause the court may extend the time prescribed to perform any act or permit an act after the time expires, but the court may not extend time to file a notice of appeal (except as authorized in Rule 4), or to file a petition for review, or for doing any act when the time has been prescribed by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court has discretion to extend most deadlines but not certain jurisdictional statutory deadlines or notice of appeal (with limited exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional time after service—5-day rule (Rule 26(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party is required or permitted to act within a prescribed period after a paper is served, five calendar days are added to the period unless the paper is delivered on the date of service stated in the proof of service. Electronically served papers are treated as delivered on the date of service stated. Rule 26(c) does not apply when an order prescribes the time or to notices of appeal filed under Rules 4, 5, or 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds 5 days for service-based deadlines (including electronic service), with enumerated exceptions.
